item.title: Seabird-Aware Multi-Objective Offshore Wind Capacity Allocation: A Gippsland Case Study
item.description: arXiv:2611.27073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Offshore wind planning requires balancing capital cost, wind-resource potential, and seabird exposure. We formulate a spatial tri-objective mixed-integer linear program for offshore wind capacity allocation, minimizing capital cost and modeled seabird exposure while maximizing wind-weighted capacity. Applied to Australia's Gippsland offshore wind area, the model identifies exposure reductions of 23-44% at capital-cost premiums of 0.8-6.1% across 15 wind-weighted capacity requirements. We benchmark exposure-aware optimization against 19 percentile-based exclusion thresholds. At a fixed wind-weighted capacity requirement, the 5th-percentile threshold reduces exposure by 30.1% at a 37.6% cost premium, versus at least 30.1% at a 1.4% premium with optimization. Under a fixed capital budget, exclusion screening reduces exposure by 48.2% with a 26.9% capacity loss, compared with 48.5% and 7.6%, respectively, under optimization. These results highlight the value of explicitly optimizing graded seabird exposure.
item.dc:creator: Leilah Taouk, Canchen Jiang, Markus Wagner, Yuqing Xiao, Yidan Zhang

item.title: Spiking Neural Networks Incrementally Track Firing-Rate Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.27322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how spiking neural networks (SNNs) efficiently process data streams is key to (i) studying how biological brains conserve energy for lifelong predictions and (ii) enabling efficient continuous AI inference. In this work, we propose a theory on how an SNN incrementally tracks its corresponding firing-rate network, a continuous-valued neural network (ANN). We prove that the output of a discrete SNN continuously tracks the instantaneous ANN output implicitly determined by the SNN input. Based on this principle, we develop LIF-Stream, a conversion framework for efficient SNN inference over unbounded data streams. It enables the converted SNN to reuse its prior activation state and compute only the activation updates between frames, thereby reducing the average number of time steps needed per frame. Specifically, LIF-Stream controls the SNN to continuously track the reference ANN output, which gives a high-accuracy prediction for every frame. Evaluation on three large-scale streaming inference benchmarks with distinct modalities shows that LIF-Stream achieves the best efficiency-accuracy trade-off compared to high-accuracy SNN techniques.
item.dc:creator: Hyunseok Oh, Youngki Lee

item.title: Grid Cells as Spectral Successor Features: A Reusable Basis for Continual Reinforcement Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.26504v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continual reinforcement learning requires agents to adapt when the task changes while reusing what they know about the environment. Successor features separate dynamics from task-specific reward, but their effectiveness depends on the choice of base features. Taking the identification of entorhinal grid cells with eigenvectors of the successor representation as a design principle, we build this basis from eigenvectors of the transition matrix of a fixed reference policy. With such a basis, the successor features at a state-action pair are a linear combination of the base features at that same pair, which is not true in general, and the coefficients are known in closed form: each successor feature is its base feature multiplied by $\theta_i = 1/(1-\gamma\lambda_i)$, where $\lambda_i$ is its eigenvalue. The long-term return is thus predicted from the same features as the immediate reward, no successor-feature network or replay buffer is needed, and adapting to a new task reduces to a linear regression on the reward. The agent acts greedily on the action values of the reference policy, which is one step of policy improvement over it and suffices to reach a single goal. In a two-goal gridworld, with the uniform random walk as reference policy, whose eigenvectors are the low-frequency Laplacian eigenvectors, agents built this way maintain near-maximal return across every change of goal, whereas SimpleSF and DQN lose most of their return at each change.
item.dc:creator: \'Elodie C\^ot\'e-Gauthier, Doina Precup, Isabeau Pr\'emont-Schwarz

item.title: On the loss landscape of the linear neural network: beyond critical points
item.description: arXiv:2611.26671v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While the critical points of the loss landscape in linear neural networks have been extensively studied since the seminal work of Baldi \& Hornik in the late 1980s, a description of this landscape at an intermediate or global scale is still lacking. Such a characterization is crucial, particularly as a substantial body of literature indicates that gradient descent circumvents critical points. The present article introduces an intermediate structure, termed the critical thalweg, which encompasses all critical points and exhibits key geometric properties. Beyond providing a geometric proof of Baldi \& Hornik's results using simpler assumptions than the existing literature, this framework offers a global view of the loss landscape that can be easily visualized in a two-dimensional plane. Empirical observations suggest that gradient descent is attracted toward the critical thalweg, along which the loss continues to decrease to its global minimum.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Lejay (PASTA, IECL), Lionel Lenotre (Universit{\'e} de Haute-Alsace), Sa{\"i}d Toubra (IECL)

item.title: MG-EDA: Maturity-Gated Skew-Normal Estimation of Distribution Algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2611.26938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gaussian estimation of distribution algorithms shrink their variance on slopes and stall far from the optimum. This paper equips the corrections that act along the direction of movement -- a mean shift, an elongation of the covariance along the path and a skewness -- with the rule they lack: a calibrated gate, driven by a maturity statistic of the population, decides whether, how strongly and for how long each correction acts, and when the gate is closed the algorithm is exactly the estimation of multivariate normal algorithm (EMNA). The statistic is a cumulative path of whitened mean shifts with an inverse-Wishart correction, whose expectation is one under a null model without systematic movement and whose quantiles give thresholds with known false-alarm rate. It gates the three corrections as three rank-one terms of one matrix sampling equation, the skewness being carried by a skew-normal sampler that preserves the estimated mean and covariance; all vanish at maturity. We call the resulting algorithm the maturity-gated EDA (MG-EDA). A full factorial study on a training set of black-box optimization benchmarking (BBOB) functions separates the parameters: variance scaling is the prerequisite, the mean shift needs a feedback correction removing the injected shift from the statistic, the elongation turns the variance loss on a slope into a gain, and the skewness substitutes for the mean shift rather than complementing it. On held-out instances MG-EDA with the first- and second-order corrections is significantly better than the skewness-only predecessor and than EMNA with variance scaling, ties with EMNA with anticipated mean shift, and trails the adapted maximum-likelihood Gaussian model (AMaLGaM) in 20 dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Jun Zhang, Tong Qian, Hua Ding, Weijie Yu, Zhi-Hui Zhan

item.title: Recurrent Amplification and Exact Nonexpansiveness Criteria for Query-Driven Erasure
item.description: arXiv:2611.27109v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Query-derived Erase Direction (QED) augments a rank-one linear attention update with a key-orthogonal query component. Under scalar decay, this correction leaves the eigenvalues of each homogeneous state transition unchanged, while the propagation of an initial perturbation depends on the ordered product of these transitions. We construct a periodic token sequence with fixed key and query projections for which every one-step spectral radius is below one but the spectral radius of the period product exceeds one. The same construction yields a sufficient condition for mean-square growth under independent uniform token sampling. For rank-one erasure with channel-wise decay, we derive a necessary and sufficient spectral-norm test for one-step nonexpansiveness that can be evaluated in $O(d)$ time. The test agrees with direct singular value decomposition on all 1,800 operators evaluated. In a counterfactual replay of a selected head of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, the terminal gain on a 4,096-token repeated-text sequence increased from 0.99938 to 1.3977 with the feature and checkpoint gate trajectories held fixed.
item.dc:creator: Haozhe Wang

item.title: Large Language Model-Driven Cooperative Operator Ensemble Evolution for Permutation Flow Shop Scheduling
item.description: arXiv:2606.15334v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The permutation flow shop scheduling problem (PFSP) is a classical NP-hard optimization problem in intelligent manufacturing. The iterated greedy (IG) metaheuristic is widely adopted for solving PFSP, due to its simplicity and strong empirical performance. However, classical IG's single fixed destruction operator often limits exploration and causes search stagnation on large, complex instances. This work proposes IG-DOE, a multi-operator IG algorithm that enhances exploration by switching among heterogeneous destruction operators along a single search trajectory. Its core mechanism, stagnation-triggered sequential switching, activates the next destruction operator in an ordered destruction operator ensemble (DOE) upon stagnation, enriching the perturbation behavior of classical IG. Moreover, to reduce reliance on expert-crafted operators, a large language model (LLM)-assisted framework, termed stagewise cooperative operator ensemble evolution (SCOE), is introduced to automatically construct a high-quality DOE through stagewise evolution, state-awareness, and cooperative evaluation. Experiments on the challenging VRF-hard-large benchmark, named after Vallada, Ruiz, and Framinan, show that the DOE evolved from smaller instances generalizes well to larger instances. Under the same CPU-time limit, IG-DOE obtained much better average performance than the Q-learning iterated greedy algorithm (QIG), a state-of-the-art IG algorithm. Further experiments on real-world industrial-data-derived instances show that the evolved DOE generalizes effectively across data distributions.
item.dc:creator: Rui Xu, Yufan Liao, Haoze Lv, Shengcai Liu, Yi Mei, Ke Tang

item.title: Growing a Neural Network in Breadth, Depth, and Time
item.description: arXiv:2605.25174v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Brains and AI systems alike must achieve their goals with limited space, time, energy, and data. Here we focus on space and time, defining differentiable costs for breadth (channels), depth (layers), and time (recurrent steps) in a recurrent convolutional network. We optimize these costs jointly with task error via backpropagation. Pricing each resource differently, we grow a diverse set of computational graphs through optimization. We find that breadth, depth, and time can be traded off against each other at a given level of accuracy. Networks grow with task complexity and, when allowed to adaptively allocate time per input, take more recurrent steps if inputs are occluded. The time the model spends on each image also correlates with human reaction times, despite no training on human data. Our work takes a step toward a normative account of how spatial and temporal resource costs jointly shape neural architectures in brains and machines.
item.dc:creator: Eivinas Butkus, Kedar Garz\'on Gupta, Nikolaus Kriegeskorte
